what_this_is: The Workshop row for the Namespace server in tools/live-namespace: the person's files on their own S3-compatible store, as MCP tools over stdio and as a WebDAV folder on a loopback port.

payload.label: Run the Namespace files server (runs on your computer)
payload.job: Serve the person's files: every name they were given, listed, read by range, written, moved, shared and released, as tools an AI calls and as a WebDAV folder Finder, a file browser or an editor mounts
payload.description: Starts the Namespace server (tools/live-namespace) over one state folder of the person's own. Mode `mcp` answers MCP over stdio: each operation of the files is a tool (list_files, find_file, read_file, read_file_span, write_file, write_file_start, write_file_piece, write_file_finish, share_file, move_names, copy_names, set_aside, put_back, queue_release, release_gone_bytes and the rest; tools/list names them all). Mode `dav` serves the WebDAV folder on 127.0.0.1 at the port in settings.json (38481 as shipped) until stopped: in Finder choose Go, Connect to Server and enter http://127.0.0.1:38481/ (macOS `mount_webdav -S http://127.0.0.1:38481/ <empty folder>` does the same). Mode `serve` is both. The names index is rows in the person's own SQL database, set by settings.json `store`: a SQLite file of that name in the state folder as shipped, or the person's Postgres database (host, port, database, user and the attached field that holds its password); the bytes live in the person's own S3-compatible store, read by the asked range only, never whole. The byte store is the person's `files-store` connection and the database's password is its own attached field: each reaches the run on the file descriptor settings.json `attached` names (files-store secret 3, key-id 4, bucket 5, endpoint 6, region 7) and is never printed, logged or written. A first run makes the files from the connection's endpoint, bucket, region and key id and the key_prefix in settings.json. The WebDAV folder answers 127.0.0.1 and localhost only and refuses a request a web page sent. share_file refuses until a delivery owner that serves a shared file's bytes is attached (it is not part of this server).

mode.description: mcp: MCP tools over stdio. dav: the WebDAV folder, until stopped. serve: both.

state_folder.description: The person's own folder for this run's working files (and the SQLite rows file, when settings.json `store` is SQLite): an absolute path in their home. It is made, readable by its owner only, when it is not there.

settings.description: Optional path to a settings file (account, WebDAV port and prefix, key prefix, attached fields), put after --settings where {settings} is in the command. Leave it out to use tools/live-namespace/settings.json.

output_schema.description: Mode mcp answers JSON-RPC lines on stdout; mode dav answers HTTP on the loopback port and prints nothing; a refusal ends the run with one line on stderr naming what was wrong, never a value of the connection.

needs: the person's files-store connection (an S3-compatible store: its secret, key id, bucket, endpoint and region), each field handed to the run on the descriptor settings.json `attached` names, read from the vault by name and never printed
the person's database: a SQLite file in the state folder, or their Postgres database and its password as an attached field, as settings.json `store` says
an empty or earlier state folder in the person's home
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer. Run it from tools/live-namespace. Give the run the files-store connection's fields (and the database password, when the rows are in Postgres) on the descriptors settings.json names (a here-string of each vault value, never echoed or logged). The first run builds and makes the files. For the Finder folder, run mode dav (or serve) and connect to http://127.0.0.1:38481/ ; for an AI, run mode mcp as the AI's stdio MCP server.

provenance.source: Trillion-X/trillion-rust src/account_files at 5fbc2ff4b1 (moved into tools/live-namespace), over its own rows in SQL (src/store)
